title: No CORRUPTION Act
official_summary:
No Congressionally Obligated Recurring Revenue Used as Pensions To Incarcerated Officials Now Act or the No CORRUPTION Act

This act makes a Member of Congress who has been convicted of a crime related to public corruption ineligible to receive retirement payments pursuant to the Civil Service Retirement System or the Federal Employees' Retirement System based on service as a Member. Under current law, a Member must forgo receipt of these payments only after a final conviction (i.e., after the exhaustion of all appeals under the judicial process).

summary.headline: Members of Congress convicted of public corruption crimes lose their congressional retirement pensions without waiting for all appeals to end.
summary.what_it_does: This law makes a Member of Congress convicted of a crime related to public corruption ineligible for retirement payments earned through their service as a Member. These payments come from the Civil Service Retirement System or the Federal Employees' Retirement System. Before this law, a Member lost these payments only after a final conviction, meaning after all appeals were used up.

who_it_affects.group: Current and former Members of Congress convicted of public corruption crimes
who_it_affects.how: They become ineligible for retirement payments based on their congressional service once convicted, rather than only after all appeals are finished.
